newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian electricity output below demand.
newsitem.headline: Serbian electricity output below demand.

text.p: Serbia has increased its power output this year but energy industry representatives said on Wednesday the rise could not meet the growing electricity needs of domestic customers.

Electricity production in January-October grew one percent to 26,962 gigawatt-hours (Gwh) from 26,733 GWh in the same period in 1995, the Department for Energy of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce said.
According to the department's report, electricity consumption jumped 23.2 percent during the same period.
Average daily electricity needs stood at around 120 million kilowatt-hours (KWh), nearly matching production capacity, the report said.
"Unlike past four years of sanctions, we are not producing sufficiently to meet a growing demand," Radoje Zecevic of the Chamber of Commerce said.
In order to meet demand, Serbian power industry "borrowed" electricity from neighbouring Bulgaria and Romania, and was not worried about rising consumption, EPS company official Aca Markovic said.
"Due to favourable hydrology in Greece and Albania, we will be able to import some electricity from those countries as well," he said.
Markovic attributed the rise in consumption to reviving industry, but said electricity consumption was not falling in the household sector either.
In order to avoid power outages, Markovic said EPS was considering the possibility of transferring electricity supply in the northern city of Subotica to the Hungarian power system.
Industry officials pointed to outdated machinery and said the latest price increase of electricity was still insufficient to cover costs.
Electricity prices were raised early in December to an average 0.23 dinars (4.5 cents) per KWh from 0.12 dinars.
The industry considers six cents per KWh as a level that would allow some money to be set aside for infrastructure maintenance and upgrading. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
